transition_semantics: transition describes entry into the current main-visual clip; any boundary with an illustration on either side must be hard_cut. Card-internal object/label entry belongs to its semantic_process, not a transition over the illustration.

illustration.identity_of_image: SHA-256 of actual source bytes; adjacent aliases are one continuous use, returning after another image/card is forbidden
illustration.scene_id_semantics: Identifies a concrete situation. Returning to a situation may reuse its scene_id but must use a new source image. Consecutive scene groups are derived separately.
illustration.scene_change_reason_semantics: Nonempty when scene_id changes from the preceding illustration, even if information cards intervene. The first illustration needs no change reason.

information_card.motion_quality: Use meaningful object relationships, traceable identity, intermediate states, arrival/occlusion and readable holds; motion=none needs an explicit simple-card purpose in the design.

narration_anchor.time_basis: episode-local frames, overlapping the clip; the same full semantic span can support several successive illustrations

opening.timing: No universal first-N-seconds or shot-count quota. Show a relevant problem/result/contrast and a reason to continue without rewriting the locked narration.

limits: This contract is the main visual sequence, not a declaration of physical editor tracks. Spoken captions are a separate overlay.
A semantic sentence can span multiple static illustrations; the 2-second cap does not cap the sentence or any information card.
Field presence, distinct hashes and a declared motion mode cannot prove meaningful visual differences, character consistency, absence of baked-in labels or actual rendered stillness.
Inspect source illustrations and actual encoded output; normal-speed picture/sound review is a separate required acceptance record for a finished video.

Scene metadata and group durations support review only: a related topic does not justify a long scene; there is no fixed scene-duration or scene-count quota. Assess visible progress and continuity across situations separately.
